newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says closely watching stock movements.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says closely watching stock movements.

text.p: The Japanese authorities are watching movements in the stock market with deep interest, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
"We will continue to watch movements in the stock market with deep interest," he said.
Asked whether the ministry was considering special measures to tackle the recent plunge in share prices, Mitsuzuka said officials would work to implement an extra budget as soon as possible.
Japan will discuss implementation of a previously planned extra budget for the current fiscal year in the next parliamentary session starting on January 20.
"The first job for us is to put in place the extra budget as soon as possible," Mitsuzuka said.

Jiji news agency reported on Tuesday that the head of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, had urged the government to consider measures to tackle the problem of weak stock prices in Tokyo.
The stock market lost more than 2,000 points last week on worries about Japan's economy and was down again at Tuesday lunchtime after having made up some lost ground on Monday.
